pair.empty: No suitable device found. Add one to Homey first, then come back.

room_sensor.title: Which sensor measures this room?
room_sensor.lead: Pick the thermometer that reads the temperature you actually care about — the one in the room, not the one built into the radiator valve. Everything the thermostat does follows from this reading.

emitter.title: What heats this room?
emitter.lead: Every radiator, valve or heater in this room. Pick more than one and they all follow the same setpoint. They must be all of one kind: either they all take a target temperature, or they are all plain on/off switches — a switched socket is driven by on time within each cycle.

boiler.title: Which switch starts the boiler?
boiler.lead: This device is turned on when enough rooms call for heat, and off as soon as none do. Check that your boiler has its own safety cut-out before letting anything drive it.

optional.title: Anything else to help it decide?
optional.lead: All of these are optional. Leave them empty and the thermostat still works — each one simply makes it smarter.
optional.outdoor_hint: Lets the algorithm anticipate heat loss instead of only reacting to it. Without it, self-regulation stays off.
optional.window_hint: Stops heating a room that is being aired, after a delay so a quick opening does not count.
optional.motion_hint: Enables the Activity preset, which follows movement in this room.
optional.presence_hint: When nobody is home, every preset falls back to its away temperature.

error.incomplete: Pick a room sensor and a heater before adding this thermostat.
error.no_api: Adaptive Thermostat cannot read your devices yet. Its access to the Homey API has not come up — reopen this in a few seconds, or restart the app.
error.repair_no_create: This device already exists — you are repairing it, not creating a new one.
error.too_many_emitters: That is more heaters than one thermostat can drive. Split the room across two thermostats instead.
error.mixed_emitters: These heaters are not of the same kind. One takes a target temperature, another is a plain on/off switch, and a thermostat drives its heaters one way or the other — not both. Group the valves together and give the switched heaters their own thermostat.

edit.title: Sources of this thermostat
edit.lead: Change any of them. Each choice takes effect immediately — the thermostat regulates on the new source from its next cycle.
edit.room_hint: The thermometer that reads the temperature you care about — the one in the room, not the one inside the radiator valve.
edit.emitter_hint: Every heater this room drives. Changing the list reloads the device: its regulation restarts from the new heaters.

settings.title: Adaptive Thermostat
settings.subtitle: The sources of your thermostats, and the optional Zigbee2MQTT backbone.

sources.title: Thermostats
sources.lead: Every thermostat reads a room sensor and drives a heater; the four other sources are optional. Change any of them here — the choice takes effect immediately, and the thermostat keeps its name, its settings, its history and its Flows.
sources.empty: No thermostat yet. Add one from Devices, then come back — its sources will be listed here.
sources.hub_offline: Your devices cannot be read right now: the app has not reached the Homey API yet. Reload in a few seconds.
sources.missing: The linked device no longer exists ({{id}}). This source is dead — pick another one.
sources.unavailable: The list of devices for this source could not be loaded.
sources.unknown_thermostat: This thermostat no longer exists. Reload the page.
sources.failed: Your thermostats could not be read: {{detail}}
sources.unknown_source: Unknown source. Reload the page and try again.
sources.invalid_device: This device cannot be used for this source. Reload the page and pick one from the list.

settings.backbone_subtitle: Optional. Unlocks direct valve control on SONOFF TRVZB and similar valves.
settings.lead: The Homey Zigbee2MQTT app does not expose everything a thermostatic valve can do: four of the properties this thermostat needs simply do not exist as Homey capabilities. If you give it access to your MQTT broker, the app publishes to Zigbee2MQTT itself and unlocks two things:
settings.lead_valve: Direct valve opening — the algorithm sets how far the valve opens, instead of steering it indirectly with a setpoint.
settings.lead_sensor: Room temperature injection — the valve regulates on your room sensor instead of its own thermometer, which sits against the radiator and always reads too warm.
settings.lead_without: Everything else works without this. Leave it off and those two features are simply unavailable — every room is still regulated, using an offset setpoint. Point this at the same broker your Zigbee2MQTT installation already uses.
settings.enabled_hint: Takes effect when the app restarts.
settings.host_hint: Host name or IP address of the broker. A scheme and a port may be included, for example mqtts://broker.local:8883. Never a username or a password — those go in the two fields below.
settings.username_hint: Leave empty if your broker accepts anonymous connections.
settings.password_hint: Leave empty if your broker accepts anonymous connections.
settings.password_stored: A password is stored. Leave this empty to keep it, or type a new one to replace it.
settings.base_topic_hint: The base topic of your Zigbee2MQTT installation. Default: zigbee2mqtt.
settings.state_unknown: State unknown — the app has not started the backbone yet.
settings.test_ok: Connected. {{count}} devices seen on this base topic.
settings.test_no_devices: Connected to the broker, but nothing arrived on <base topic>/bridge/devices. The base topic is almost certainly wrong.
settings.test_auth_failed: The broker refused the credentials. Check the username and the password.
settings.test_refused: The broker could not be reached ({{detail}}). Check the address and the port.
settings.test_timeout: No answer from the broker within ten seconds. Check the address and the port, and that the broker is reachable from Homey.
settings.test_invalid_config: These settings are incomplete or invalid. Check the address, the port and the base topic.
settings.test_unknown: The test returned an unexpected answer.

linked.missing: Device no longer exists — set it again in the app settings

settings.test_host_has_credentials: Do not put a username or a password in the address. Use the two fields below — they are the only ones that keep the password out of the logs.

explain.away_hint: When the presence sensor reports an empty home, each preset falls back to the temperature below instead of its normal one. The preset shown on the tile does not change — only what the thermostat aims for. Without a presence sensor, these values are never used.
explain.boiler_hint: The app counts how many emitters are calling for heat across the home and switches the relay when enough of them are. Driving a real boiler carries a risk: one running against closed valves builds pressure. Check that yours has its own safety cut-out before letting anything switch it.
explain.central_hint: The Boiler device carries one switch for the whole home — everything off, heating only, or frost protection — and the relay that starts your boiler. The two settings below decide whether this thermostat obeys that switch, and whether its demand counts towards starting the boiler. Both are on by default. Turn the first off for a room you want to keep controlling by hand; turn the second off for a heater that has nothing to do with the boiler, such as an electric radiator.
explain.emitter_hint: The app drives whatever it can: a setpoint, a valve opening, or a plain switch. The valve settings below only apply when the Zigbee2MQTT backend is configured in the app settings — valve opening is not something Homey exposes on its own.
explain.expert_hint: These values replace the preset self-regulation modes when you choose Expert above. They are the raw coefficients of the correction; the preset modes are just named combinations of them. If you have not deliberately chosen Expert, nothing here has any effect.
explain.presence_hint: Presence is about the home: nobody there, every preset falls back to its away temperature. Motion is about this room only, and drives the Activity preset — which is offered only once all four settings below are filled in.
explain.presets_hint: The temperature this thermostat aims for under each preset. Presets are how you drive it day to day — from a Flow, from the tile, or from a schedule — instead of typing a number each time.
explain.regulation_hint: A radiator valve measures the radiator, not the room — it reads warm and closes too early. Self-regulation offsets the setpoint sent to it so the room reaches your target. It needs an outdoor temperature sensor: without one, no offset is applied at all.
explain.safety_hint: A flat battery in January would otherwise leave the room unheated until someone notices: the app refuses to compute on a frozen reading, so it stops asking for heat. Instead, it keeps a minimum going until the sensor comes back — and gives up after the delay below, because a boiler running for days on a dead sensor is a bigger risk than the frost it was avoiding.
explain.tpi_hint: This is what separates a real thermostat from a bimetallic strip. Instead of switching fully on and fully off, the app computes how much heat the room actually needs and delivers exactly that. The defaults suit a normally insulated room; change them only if you observe a problem.
explain.window_hint: Two ways to notice, and they are mutually exclusive. A contact sensor is immediate and reliable. Detection by temperature drop needs no sensor at all but reacts more slowly, and only once the app has enough readings to measure a slope.

device.no_emitter: No heater is linked. Use Repair to pick one.
device.central_duplicate: A Boiler device already exists. Only one is allowed — delete this one.
device.sync_restart: Saved. The write-interval settings for the emitter take effect when the app restarts.

warning.no_sensor: No usable room temperature sensor: regulation is suspended and nothing is being sent to the heater.
warning.sensor_stale: The room temperature reading is stale: regulation is suspended and nothing is being sent to the heater.
warning.sensor_stale_safety: The room temperature reading is stale. Safety mode holds a fallback heating level until the sensor comes back, then it gives up.
warning.valve_stuck: The Zigbee2MQTT backbone went away and the valve stayed at its last opening: the room may not heat whatever the setpoint says. Regulation continues by setpoint.
